title: Threads and mutex
learningGoals: start a thread and join it
protect shared data with a mutex

youtube.title: C++ Threads and Mutex: Concurrency Basics | C++ Programming EP 87
youtube.description: In this episode you will start a thread and join it, share data between threads and protect shared data with a mutex, with Xecxec the crab. 0:00 Intro · 0:15 Threads and mutex · 1:19 Start and join a thread · 2:23 Start, work, join · 2:53 Second program · 4:29 Recap · 5:01 Bug of the Day · 5:49 Challenge · 6:16 Next episode

scenes.animation: Tomato title card: EP sticker thuds in, title stamps with a whoosh, Xecxec scuttles in and waves; thud, whoosh, claw-click, sting
scenes.narration: Today we run code on two threads at once. We also learn the lock that keeps shared data safe.

scenes.onScreen: "Threads and mutex": numbered lines (1. A thread runs code at the same time; 2. Join waits for a thread to finish; 3. A mutex lets one thread in at a time) and an analogy card: two cooks in one kitchen, and a key to the pantry
scenes.animation: Lines spring in one by one with a pop; the analogy card slides in from the right
scenes.narration: A thread is a second path of execution. Two threads can run at the same time. You must join each thread before it goes out of scope. When two threads change the same data, they can clash. A mutex is a key. Only the thread that holds the key may enter. Think of two cooks and one pantry. Today a laptop has many cores. A program with threads can use them all at once. Threads share memory, which makes them powerful and dangerous. Two threads that write to one variable can overwrite each other. This is called a data race, and it gives wrong answers that change from run to run.
points: A thread runs code at the same time
Join waits for a thread to finish
A mutex lets one thread in at a time

scenes.onScreen: thread.cpp: a thread adds numbers, and main joins it
scenes.animation: Code types in with key-tick; butter [HL n] highlight sweeps line by line with marker-swipe; explanation card on the right
scenes.narration: [HL 7] This line starts a new thread. The thread runs the lambda at once. [HL 7] The lambda captures result by reference, so it can change the variable of main. [HL 9] It adds the numbers from one to one hundred. [HL 12] Join makes main wait until the thread is done. [HL 13] Now it is safe to read result. The sum is five thousand and fifty. [HL 7] A thread starts at once, and it runs the lambda. The capture with an ampersand lets the lambda change result. [HL 12] Join waits until the thread is finished. Without it, main might print before the thread has done its work. [HL 13] The sum of one to one hundred is five thousand and fifty.

scenes.onScreen: a flow: main starts a thread, both run, main joins
scenes.animation: Steps drop in left to right with a pop; connecting arrows draw on; the active step glows butter
scenes.narration: Main starts the thread. The thread does the work. Main waits at join. Only after the join does main read the result. Notice the two paths in the picture. Main and the thread run side by side, and the join is the point where they meet again.

diagram.caption: a flow: main starts a thread, both run, main joins

scenes.onScreen: mutex.cpp: two threads add to one counter, guarded by a mutex
scenes.animation: Second program or a twist on the first; [HL n] and [TRACK name=value] cues drive the variable tracker; output panel fills line by line with a ding per line
scenes.narration: [HL 8] The mutex is the key to the pantry. [HL 9] Both threads run this same lambda. Each one adds one to the counter, one thousand times. [HL 11] Lock guard takes the key. It gives the key back at the end of each pass. While one thread holds the key, the other thread waits. [HL 12] So the two threads never change the counter together. [HL 17] Main joins both threads. The counter is two thousand every time. [HL 8] The mutex is the key to the counter. [HL 11] The lock guard takes the key when it is made. It gives the key back when it dies at the end of the round. [HL 15] Two threads run the same work. [HL 19] Each thread adds one thousand, so the answer is always two thousand.

scenes.animation: Dark-blue terminal: the compile command types with key-tick, the run command types, output prints in mint with a ding
scenes.narration: Save the file as mutex dot cpp. Compile it with g plus plus. Then run the program. The program prints five thousand and fifty, and then two thousand. Notice that the answer is the same on every run. Without the lock, it could be lower.

scenes.animation: Recap lines tick in one by one with a pop; Xecxec nods after each tick
scenes.narration: Let us recap. One. A thread runs code at the same time as main. Two. Join waits for a thread to finish. Three. Two threads that change the same data need a mutex. Four. Lock guard gives the key back for you. Pause the video. Say these ideas out loud, one time, slowly.
points: A thread runs code at the same time as main.
Join waits for a thread to finish.
Two threads that change the same data need a mutex.
Lock guard gives the key back for you.

scenes.onScreen: BUG OF THE DAY: A thread that is never joined
scenes.animation: Butter banner drops in with a buzzer; the program crashes and the run-time error appears in tomato; the fix slides in and the output turns mint with a ding
scenes.narration: Bug of the Day. We start a thread and never join it. The program stops with terminate called without an active exception. Join every thread before main ends. A thread object that is still joinable when it dies ends the whole program. Always call join before the end of the scope. Or detach the thread, if you want it to run alone.

scenes.onScreen: Why did two threads share one door? They took turns, because one had the key.
scenes.animation: Full tomato screen, card flips in with a rimshot, Xecxec snaps his claw
scenes.narration: Why did two threads share one door? They took turns, because one had the key.

scenes.animation: Task card pops in; checklist ticks with a pop; Xecxec holds a tiny pen
scenes.narration: Your challenge: Start two threads. Each thread adds half of a vector into its own variable. Join both, and print the total. Hint: give each thread its own sum variable, so the two threads never touch the same data. Write your answer in the comments.

bug.why: A thread that goes out of scope while it is still joinable ends the program. Always join the thread, or detach it on purpose.

challengeAnswer: Make two result variables. Each thread adds its own half into its own variable. After both joins, add the two results.
